It comprises disparagement of Satan [Iblis] for his vanity and his refusing to prostrate before Adam (peace be upon him), and his being the first to display bigotry and to act through vanity; it comprises a warning to people treading in Satan’s path.

key_terms.الْقَاصِعَة: The Sermon of Disparagement (a specific sermon in Nahj al-Balagha)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Satan's refusal to prostrate to Adam in the Sermon of Disparagement?
ai.summary: In this sermon, Imam Ali (AS) identifies Satan’s refusal to prostrate to Adam not merely as disobedience, but as the primordial root of tribalism (al-‘asabiyyah) and pride (al-ḥamiyyah), a concept central to Shia political theology. This narrative establishes the spiritual and social consequences of ego, linking the cosmic rebellion to human societal divisions. It serves as a timeless warning against the subtle corruption of self-importance that leads to deviation from divine command.

en.sayed-ali-raza: It comprises disparagement of Satan [Iblīs] for his vanity and his refusing to prostrate before Adam [a.s.], and his being the first to display bigotry and to act through vanity; it comprises a warning to people treading in Satan’s path.
